Following the execution path, we find that the error occurs at line 49 of `tests/test_types.py`, where it tries to assert that the list returned by `list(seq)` is empty. This assertion fails with an `IndexError: list index out of range` exception.

The call stack indicates that this exception originates from the `thefuck/types.py` file, specifically from line 106 and later line 85. Upon closer inspection, we see that these lines are part of the `__iter__` method of the `SortedCorrectedCommandsSequence` class.

From the code snippets provided by the `get_code_snippet` function calls, we can infer that the `_realise()` method is responsible for realising the sequence's internal state. This method seems to be called when the iterator (`self._cached`) has not been realised before.

However, upon further inspection of the `__init__` method (line 63-66), we notice that a call to `_realise_first()` initializes the `_cached` list with the result of calling `_realise()`. 

Moreover, in line 105, it is stated that if self._realised is False, _realise() will be called. In this case, we have an empty list (`[]`) which leads us to understand that `self._commands` hasn't been populated (line 64). When the `_realise()` method tries to access the first element of `self._cached` in line 106, it results in an out-of-range error.

This is because when we pass an empty list (`[]`) to `SortedCorrectedCommandsSequence`, its internal state is not correctly set up for iteration. The test fails as a result because the iterator (`self._cached`) has no valid elements to return, thus causing an `IndexError`.

Conclusion: The test `test_with_blank` checks whether an empty list is correctly processed by the `SortedCorrectedCommandsSequence` class. However, due to the internal state not being correctly set up for iteration when passing an empty list (`[]`) as argument in its constructor, it results in an `IndexError`. 

The best locations to fix this bug are: 
```
thefuck.types.SortedCorrectedCommandsSequence.__init__(self, commands, settings)
thefuck.types._iter__
```
